original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: In CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's explicit F2[UT4(F2)] central-target alphabet (paid factors I+([g]+1)xy^T, g in {a,b,c}, target I+([z]+1)I_2), prove that no legal two-target word of any finite length on any finite restored dirty workspace can have n_b=7 with middle ranks (rank X, rank Y)=(2,2), under the same e_b=0-style unrestricted side-zero profile reduction used by #3887. Explicitly leave middle-rank patterns (2,3) and (3,2), and unrestricted n_b=7, open. Do not claim every n_b=7 word is impossible.
scope_change_reason: Follows #3887 (n_b=6 exclusion) and open next question 2 of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1816 (research/ut4-two-target-fifteen). Packages only the finished rank pattern (2,2) of the length-7 unrestricted-profile census; mixed ranks (2,3)/(3,2) were not finished and stay open.
bottleneck_link: After #3887 every realizing word has n_b>=7; excluding the (2,2) slice at n_b=7 under the same unrestricted-profile reduction narrows the remaining weighted-tariff gate. Screening/quotient result only; no supplier or kappa change. Selected decimal stays 0.001672660197076918.
stop_rule: Stop after deciding the n_b=7 middle-ranks-(2,2) case (exhibit or prove none under the #3887 reduction). Leave (2,3), (3,2), and unrestricted n_b=7 open. Do not claim full n_b=7 impossibility. Do not reopen three-target lengths 21/22 or unit-tariff minimum 16.
evidence: PROOF.md: at n_b=7 with rank X=rank Y=2 all seven b-couplings lie in the active 2-plane, so abc/cba and the a/b and c/b side coefficients receive no interior dirty contraction and reduce to the two-role unrestricted side-zero profile equations (same reduction as #3887). core.py/verify.py: all 49686 GL2-minimal zero-sum 7-middles; 49140 with ranks exactly (2,2); every side-zero profile's transport keys; 0 pairs with abc=cba=I. independent.py repeats the census with a separate base-16 MITM. Low-rank control (ranks (1,2)) still finds pairs, so the screen is not vacuous. Patterns (2,3), (3,2) and unrestricted n_b=7 left open.
author: Wentao Li <wentaol4@illinois.edu>
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance in search design, proof writing, packaging and verification; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Does any two-target word have n_b=7 with middle ranks (2,3) or (3,2)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those patterns saturate n_b = 2 + rank X + rank Y and require dirty roles beyond the two-plane reduction used here; together with this (2,2) exclusion they would decide all of n_b=7.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the profile/key analysis to r>=3 with one middle excess role, or find an algebraic obstruction for (2,3)/(3,2).
open_questions.blocked_by: Middle excess when rank X or Y is 3 needs a dirty-role argument beyond the unrestricted two-role e_b=0-style reduction; 16^7 two-role profiles do not cover that case.

open_questions.question: Is every n_b=7 two-target word impossible (unrestricted over middle ranks)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Finishes the first step of #1816 open question 2 on weighted tariffs versus (abcb)^2 once (2,3) and (3,2) are decided.
open_questions.first_step: Combine this (2,2) exclusion with a (2,3)/(3,2) argument; do not treat the present package as that claim.
